item.title: Highlights of Chinese premier's speech at Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
HANGZHOU, Sept. 24 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Thursday addressed the launching ceremony of the Fifth Global Digital Trade Expo in Hangzhou, Zhejiang Province. The following are some highlights of his remarks: -- Every major technological innovation in history brought about a more open world. Today, with accelerated digitization, the trend of economic globalization is unstoppable. Against this backdrop, mutual distrust and beggar-thy-neighbor approach will only be discarded by the times, and only through mutual trust, mutual benefit and open cooperation can we win the future. -- The international community should enhance North-South cooperation in the field of digital trade, and provide more support to developing countries in terms of technology, infrastructure and personnel training. Development needs to have both speed and a human touch if we are to realize global prosperity and better life for all. -- For many years, China has been steadfastly promoting economic globalization. We honor our commitments, strengthen cooperation, uphold equality and pursue win-win outcomes. This way, we achieve development at home and benefit the wider world at the same time. In the digital era, China will continue to embrace the world, deepen economic and trade cooperation with all parties, and jointly promote global economic recovery and growth. -- Companies are an important force in driving digital trade. We warmly welcome more rigorous investment from companies of all countries and their long-term commitment in the Chinese market. We will fully implement national treatment for foreign-invested enterprises, resolve their reasonable concerns, and enable them to run and grow their business with confidence.

item.title: Xi says he is confident China, U.S. can find right way to get along
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
WASHINGTON, Sept. 23 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday voiced confidence that China and the United States, as two major countries, can find a right way to get along in the new era. This year is a crucial year for the respective development of China and the United States, Xi said in a written speech upon his arrival for a U.S. state visit. Xi noted that he and U.S. President Donald Trump agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability during Trump's visit to China in May, which has provided strategic guidance for the future development of bilateral ties. China and the United States should work in the same direction, promote a stable relationship featuring cooperation as the mainstay, moderate competition, manageable differences, and promises of peace, Xi said.

item.title: Xi lands in U.S. for state visit, greeted by Trump at airport
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
Xi lands in U.S. for state visit, greeted by Trump at airport Updated: September 24, 2026 11:15Xinhua WASHINGTON, Sept. 23 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping arrived at Joint Base Andrews on Wednesday afternoon for a state visit to the United States at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump. Xi and his wife, Peng Liyuan, were warmly greeted by Trump and his wife, Melania Trump, at the airport in a rare planeside welcome. American children presented flowers to Xi and Peng. The honor guards lined up on both sides of the red carpet to pay their respects. The welcome ceremony also included a 21-gun salute, the playing of the national anthems of both countries and a military flyover. In a written speech, Xi extended sincere greetings and best wishes to the U.S. people on behalf of the Chinese people. China and the United States are both great countries, and the two peoples are both great peoples, Xi said in the speech, adding that the two peoples have maintained friendly exchanges for a long time and their interests are deeply intertwined. China and the United States should be partners, not rivals, he said, noting that the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation and making America great again can go hand in hand, and that the two countries can help each other succeed and advance the well-being of the whole world. Xi noted that he and Trump agreed to build a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability during Trump's visit to China in May, which has provided strategic guidance for the future development of bilateral ties. China and the United States should work in the same direction, promote a stable relationship featuring cooperation as the mainstay, moderate competition, manageable differences, and promises of peace, Xi said. He said China and the United States, as two major countries, should find a right way to get along in the new era. Xi emphasized that the world is developing and times are changing, but the historical logic of peaceful coexistence between China and the United States has not changed, the goodwill of friendly exchanges between the two peoples has not changed, and the general expectations of the international community for China and the United States have not changed. Xi said he looks forward to having in-depth exchanges with Trump on major issues concerning bilateral relations and the world situation, constantly enriching the connotation of the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, and expanding the space for exchanges and cooperation in various fields between the two countries. Xi said he also looks forward to engaging extensively with people from all walks of life in the United States to deepen friendship. With joint efforts, Xi said he believes the visit is sure to be fruitful, and will enhance the well-being of the two peoples and add hope for world peace. On Xi's way from the airport to his hotel by car, representatives of overseas Chinese and students gathered on both sides of the road, waving the national flags of China and the United States to warmly welcome his visit.

item.title: Chinese vice premier calls for advancing rural revitalization
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
WUHAN, Sept. 23 -- Chinese Vice Premier Liu Guozhong has called for mobilizing efforts across society to build a beautiful and harmonious countryside for people to live and work in and steadily advance rural revitalization. Liu, who is also a member of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, visited central China's Hubei Province from Monday to Wednesday, and attended a national event in celebration of the ninth Chinese farmers' harvest festival. In Xiangyang's Xiangzhou and Zaoyang, Liu inspected autumn grain production, agricultural machinery services and rural environmental improvement, and joined farmers in celebrating the harvest festival. This year, China has overcome adverse factors, including natural disasters, to achieve a record summer grain harvest, maintain stable early rice output, and put the autumn grain harvest on track for a bumper crop, he noted. Liu called for strengthening late-season management of autumn grain crops and disaster prevention and reduction, and ensuring well-organized harvesting and grain purchases. He also urged efforts to develop high-standard farmland, develop distinctive rural industries, and expand channels for farmers to increase their incomes. In Shiyan's Danjiangkou, Liu inspected water source protection and water diversion projects. He called for stronger water source protection, safe project operation and reliable water quality, along with strict controls on construction quality and production safety, stronger oversight of funds, and faster development of a modern water network. The Chinese farmers' harvest festival is the first national festival created specifically for the country's farmers. Launched in 2018, the festival coincides with the Autumnal Equinox each year, which is one of the 24 solar terms of the Chinese lunisolar calendar and usually falls between Sept. 22 and 24, during the country's agricultural harvest season.

item.title: Chinese premier addresses opening ceremony of WorldSkills Conference 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-23
SHANGHAI, Sept. 23 -- Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Wednesday addressed the opening ceremony of the WorldSkills Conference 2026 held in Shanghai, calling for closer international exchanges and cooperation on skills development. China's development achievements embody prominent contributions of skills, Li said, noting that traditional Chinese skills have been passed down through generations and many of them have reached the world, empowering talent cultivation and industrial development in various countries, while promoting mutual understanding and cultural integration. Li stressed that China has always been committed to cultivating skills advantages among workers and focusing on the deep integration of industry and skills, and will advance industry-education integration and school-enterprise cooperation in the future. Noting that the new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation is profoundly reshaping skills demand, Li called for all parties to adapt to the times, strengthen collaboration and strive to boost global skills development. The premier also called for actively carrying out general education on AI, helping workers achieve skills transformation and promoting high-quality sufficient employment. Calling for establishing closer international skills exchange and cooperation mechanisms, Li said China is ready to work with all parties to build the global skills innovation center, strengthen skills development under the Belt and Road Initiative and through South-South cooperation. Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and President of WorldSkills International Francis Hourant attended the opening ceremony and delivered speeches. The opening ceremony was also attended by about 1,900 representatives from around the world. The 48th WorldSkills Competition opened in Shanghai on Tuesday evening, with 1,385 competitors from 68 countries and regions vying in 64 skill events. The WorldSkills Conference 2026 and the WorldSkills Shanghai 2026 Expo were held alongside the competition. Competition events will conclude on Sept. 27.

item.title: China, Kazakhstan vow to deepen pragmatic cooperation
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 22 -- Chinese Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang met with Kazakhstan's First Deputy Prime Minister Nurlybek Nalibayev in Beijing on Tuesday afternoon, and both sides agreed to deepen pragmatic cooperation. Ding, also a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, said China and Kazakhstan are good neighbors, good friends and good partners linked by mountains and rivers and sharing a common future. In July this year, the two heads of state held a meeting, charting the course for the development of bilateral relations and the deepening of practical cooperation, Ding said. "As co-chairs of the China-Kazakhstan cooperation committee, we should fully implement the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state, give full play to the committee's role in overall coordination, and promote new outcomes in practical cooperation in key areas such as trade and investment, artificial intelligence and green minerals, so as to better enhance the well-being of the two peoples," Ding said. Nalibayev said Kazakhstan is willing to follow the strategic guidance of the two heads of state and work with China to further develop close and fruitful cooperation and bring Kazakhstan-China relations to a higher level.

item.title: Xi sends congratulatory letter to 48th WorldSkills Competition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-22
BEIJING, Sept. 22 -- Chinese President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter on Tuesday to the 48th WorldSkills Competition. Xi noted that a new round of scientific and technological revolution and industrial transformation is advancing rapidly, exerting a profound impact on global skills development. Closely aligned with the needs of industries, the WorldSkills Competition provides a useful platform for skilled professionals from various countries to hone their skills and learn from each other, Xi said. Xi stressed that China will take the opportunity of hosting this year's competition to encourage and guide more workers, especially young people, to pursue a path to success through skills. "China is willing to strengthen exchanges and cooperation with all parties, promote the development of the WorldSkills movement, and better contribute to global economic growth and the improvement of people's well-being," Xi said. The 48th WorldSkills Competition opened in Shanghai the same day under the theme "Master Skills Change Your Future." Hosted by WorldSkills International and jointly organized by China's Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the Shanghai Municipal People's Government, the competition will also feature the WorldSkills Conference and WorldSkills Expo.

item.title: China tightens accountability for officials regarding ecological, environmental damage
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-26
BEIJING, Aug. 25 -- Chinese officials found responsible for serious ecological and environmental damage will be held accountable for life, even if they have since left their posts, according to a recently released policy document. Issued by the General Office of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, the document outlines the cases that can lead to official accountability, as well as the disciplinary measures that may follow. The accountability framework was originally released in 2015. An official with the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee said an update was necessary as China has entered a stage of high-quality development featuring accelerated green and low-carbon growth, while the CPC Central Committee has issued a series of new requirements on ecological and environmental protection in recent years. The revised rules broaden the scope of accountability beyond leading Party and government officials to include senior officials at public institutions, development zones and state-owned enterprises. China has pledged to bring carbon dioxide emissions to a peak before 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality before 2060. The revised document specifies that local officials who fail to effectively advance these efforts will also be held accountable. Meanwhile, the official from the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee noted that accountability for ecological and environmental damage must be precise and evidence-based. "It should neither dampen officials' enthusiasm for work, nor undermine the credibility of the Party and the government." China has stepped up ecological and environmental protection efforts. During the second round of the central ecological and environmental protection inspections, conducted from May 2020 to June 2022, a total of 3,371 people were held accountable. The third round of such inspections is currently underway. The revised accountability rules also bring them into line with China's Ecological and Environmental Code, which officially took effect on Aug. 15.
